references.prompt: Mountain massif tile: one single solid diorama tile shaped like seven regular hexagons fused together into a honeycomb cluster, seven hexagons, a centre and six around it, the outer border an 18-sided zig-zag outline of eighteen straight flat sides each 16 m long, with twelve outward-pointing corners and six inward notches, not a plain hexagon and not a circle, about 84 m across, the whole tile centred in frame with plain grey margin all round. The top is one continuous landscape with no grid lines, grooves, gaps or seams between the seven hexagons, so the hexagons show only in the zig-zag outline, and the hexagon side walls show a thin grass lip over dark root-filled topsoil that darkens softly downward into a near-black foot, one continuous dark earth, the same shallow depth all the way round, with no rock in the side walls. Over the central hexagon rises one broad weathered granite dome about 20 m high, its smooth rounded grassy shoulders swelling gently up out of the meadow across the six surrounding hexagons, crowned by three granite tors of huge rounded blocks stacked like piled cushions, with aprons of pale grey scree and loose fallen boulders spilling down the slopes below the tors, every rock weathered pale grey granite speckled with darker grey and black flecks, softly rounded by weather with a few sharp fractured faces and shallow cracks, patches of pale green-grey and mustard-yellow lichen and a little dark moss in the crevices on the shaded side, the stone reading as a matte surface. All the way round inside the zig-zag rim runs a band of flat open meadow about 10 m wide, level with the rim on every side, lush dense clumpy meadow grass with a few small wildflowers, one even fresh green from the rim to the foot of the slopes with no lighter or darker band. The slopes, rock and scree all start inside that band, and none of them reaches the rim or the side walls. The whole tile is a clean photoreal 3D computer graphics render, stylized-real diorama miniature, real PBR materials, slightly exaggerated proportions, soft noon sun, neutral grey studio background, high camera looking down at about 65 degrees elevation so the whole zig-zag outline of the seven hexagons reads clearly, the dark earth side walls visible along the front
